entries.proposition: DESIGN: MIN6 cells exposed to 100 nM epinephrine for 3 days, then 2 days without it; the epinephrine was obtained from an animal hospital; transcriptome n of 3 per group; Student t-tests; no antagonist, no receptor knockdown, no vehicle-matched oxidation control.
entries.snippet: Epinephrine for cell culture was obtained from the Animal Hospital of Southwest University, and the concentration used in this study was 100 nM.

entries.proposition: NO ROS ASSAY: the Methods list kits for total antioxidant capacity, SOD, catalase, glutathione peroxidase and ATP; there is no ROS probe, yet the Discussion concludes that prolonged epinephrine leads to increased ROS production.
entries.snippet: In conclusion, prolonged exposure to epinephrine leads to increased ROS production.

entries.proposition: The kit list in the Methods: total antioxidant capacity, superoxide dismutase, catalase, glutathione peroxidase and ATP content; nothing that measures reactive oxygen species.
entries.snippet: Total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC assay kit, A015-3), superoxide dismutase box (SOD assay kit, A001-3-2), catalase (CAT assay kit, A007-1), glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px assay kit, A005-1-2), and ATP content

entries.proposition: NO APOPTOSIS ASSAY: the Introduction says apoptosis was measured; the Methods contain no apoptosis assay, Bax was unchanged and Bcl2 fell by a third in the qPCR.
entries.snippet: we measured insulin secretion, cell proliferation, and apoptosis in MIN6 cells

entries.proposition: DESENSITISATION is inferred from the alpha2A receptor mRNA, which fell by 13 percent at day 3 and about 30 percent at day 5 (Figure 1B); no receptor protein, cAMP or signalling readout is reported.
entries.snippet: Despite removal of epinephrine, α2A-AR RNA expression did not show reversible features (Figure 1B).

entries.proposition: TIMING: glucose-stimulated secretion was measured on day 5, after two days without epinephrine, not during exposure; the Discussion contrasts it with reports that secretion decreased after 72 hours of exposure.
entries.snippet: In contrast to the acute epinephrine response mechanism, insulin secretion decreased rather than increased when MIN6 cells were exposed to epinephrine for 72 h [21,22]

entries.proposition: MITOCHONDRIA: the text reads upregulated electron-transport and ATP-synthase subunits as disruption of ATP synthesis, while ATP content doubled at 20 mM glucose in the treated cells (Figure 5A).
entries.snippet: the levels of ETC and ATP synthase subunits were upregulated, indicating a disruption in mitochondria ATP synthesis (Figure 4B)

entries.proposition: PSEUDOREPLICATION RISK: docked insulin granules were counted in at least six random sections per group, a section count and not independent culture replicates.
entries.snippet: at least six random sections were used per group, and vesicles with dense bodies within 0.2 μm of the plasma membrane were considered to be docked insulin granules

entries.proposition: The Introduction cites an association of elevated fetal catecholamines with neonatal hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia (source 14); the experiment itself uses an adult mouse insulinoma line, not a neonatal system.
entries.snippet: elevated fetal catecholamines are associated with neonatal β-cell physiology, suggesting a mechanistic link between prenatal or perinatal stress and subsequent neonatal hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia

entries.proposition: Figure 1: (B) alpha2A receptor mRNA relative fold change about 0.87 at day 3 and 0.70 at day 5; (C) glucose-stimulated insulin secretion rises at 20 mM glucose only (about 6.5 to 9.5); (D) insulin content about 37 to 50.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1 panels B, C and D: bars of alpha2A-AR mRNA fold change (control 1.0, chronic epinephrine about 0.87 and 0.70 with asterisks), insulin secretion at 0, 2.8, 10 and 20 mM glucose with an asterisk only at 20 mM, total insulin content with an asterisk.
